llm_proposer.assessment: The alarm is caused most likely by a local gain collapse in oms.S11-S12.amp4. Its input power and pump current remained unchanged while its output fell about 8.5 dB, with the same loss propagating through downstream amplifiers and appearing across all monitored channels at S12.

proposals.rationale: The unchanged amp4 input combined with an approximately 8.5 dB output reduction and AMP_GAIN_OOR directly identifies loss of gain in amp4; downstream amp5/amp6 inputs and outputs show the propagated deficit. The unchanged pump-current reading is the only mild counterpoint, but gain can fall without a detected pump-current change.

proposals.rationale: A gain-control defect at amp4 could include spectral tilt and produce reduced channel powers downstream. However, essentially every channel at S12 fell by a similar 8.3–8.6 dB, favoring broadband gain drop rather than band-edge-selective tilt.

Noise-figure degradation could explain the broad downstream OSNR deterioration. It should leave amplifier output power approximately normal, contrary to the measured 8.48 dB output-power loss at amp4.
